# F2 — Profile remaining Herdr refresh cost drivers

## Background

The intake brief lists known large-DB cost candidates but none are yet
profiled rigorously: `wl sync` ≈ 36 s (git push/network vs JSONL export vs DB
compaction?), `wl list`/`wl worklist` spawn RSS ~130–145 MB, per-expand
`wl dep list` / single-parent `wl list --parent` spawns, and the in-process
SQLite open cost (~46–70 ms FTS DDL). Parent AC 1–6 need per-driver numbers and
a decision on what is in scope vs. a separate `wl sync` perf item (intake
scope-creep guard: "record a linked child, don't absorb"). Uses the F1 harness.

## Target outcome

A ranked, evidence-backed cost table for one full refresh (event → data load →
render) plus a `wl sync` breakdown, with a decision per driver: in-scope fix
(feeds F3–F6) or separate work item (created with a blocker edge).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A measured cost table (wall time and CPU time, using the F1 harness at full
  scale) attributing refresh cost across: `wl worklist` payload build + JSON
  parse, in-process SQLite open (DDL/FTS) + queries, per-expand child/dep
  reads, hydrator per-item `wl dep list` spawns, and render. Each row states
  measured value, cost driver, and recommended action (fix-in-scope / separate
  item / no-op).
- A `wl sync` profile on a ≥ 100 MB DB breaking the ~36 s into: git fetch/push
  (network), JSONL export, DB compaction/wal checkpoint, and CLI overhead.
  Conclusion explicitly marks whether a `wl sync` perf fix is required and
  whether it is in-scope here or a new work item per the intake guardrail. If a
  separate item is warranted, it is created with a blocking dependency recorded
  on this item — this item itself does NOT absorb a `wl sync` fix.
- Confirmed memory breakdown for a `wl worklist` / `wl list` spawn (~130–145 MB
  peak): full JSON materialisation vs enrichments vs SQLite read cache. States
  whether the payload can be trimmed without changing the documented `wl
  worklist` payload contract (feeding F5's decision).
- The report is recorded as a comment on this item with exact re-runnable
  commands, timestamps, and the reference-host path.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add/reuse the F1 harness for full-scale sampling of each refresh stage
  (probe points via existing spawn accounting and scope helpers).
- Profile `wl sync` with `time -v` / `--loglevel`, git dry-run and
  `git count-objects`/pack inspection, and DB pragma checks (`page_count`,
  `journal_mode`, wal size).
- Triage `wl list`/worklist RSS with `node --cpu-prof`/`--heapsnapshot` or
  `--trace-gc` on the CLI entry; attribute to payload vs enrichment.
- Write the report comment and, if warranted, `wl create` the separate `wl
  sync` perf child with `wl dep add <sync-item> <this-item>`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — full-scale sampling driver.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — spawn accounting / probe points.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` and `src/sync.ts` — `wl sync` pipeline to profile.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — payload build to profile/mem-diagnose.

## Deliverables

- Ranked cost table + sync breakdown comment, decision record, and (if
  required) a separate linked `wl sync` perf work item.

## Dependencies

- F1 (harness and baseline).

# F3 — Auto-sync isolation: pane never stalls on `wl sync`

## Background

Auto-sync spawns `wl sync` (≈ 36 s on a ~100 MB DB) fire-and-forget every 60 s.
Parent AC 3 requires that while a long sync is in flight the pane stays
responsive: no lock wait, no event-loop stall, no "hanging" indication beyond a
brief non-blocking status notice. The current single-flight + heartbeat +
`--if-idle` guards (auto-sync.ts) bound spawns but do not yet guarantee the
pane never competes with or waits on a long-running sync (IO contention with
refresh reads, process-group/PID effects, no UI notice). F2 profiles where the
~36 s goes and whether a `wl sync` fix is a separate item (scope guard).

## Target outcome

A refresh completes within budget while a long `wl sync` is in flight in the
background, with a non-blocking status notice shown; the pane never waits on
the sync lock or its process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a simulated/hooked long ~36 s `wl sync` in flight (F1 harness), a
  concurrent default-view refresh completes within the parent AC 2 budget and
  blocks the TUI event loop ≤ 200 ms aggregate (parent AC 1); asserted by an
  automated test in the default suite.
- The auto-sync spawn is verified off the TUI event loop and the pane shows a
  non-blocking status notice ("syncing…") that never blocks input; no "hanging"
  UI state beyond the notice (parent AC 3).
- No lock contention: an in-flight sync does not hold/reset the same SQLite
  handle or filesystem lock the pane's in-process refresh scope uses; a refresh
  never waits for a sync to finish (asserted with in-flight instrumentation:
  e.g. start time monotonic, no wait gap equal to remaining sync time).
- Existing guarantees preserved: single-flight, cross-pane heartbeat skip,
  `--if-idle`, 60 s interval, no concurrent sync spawns (parent AC 6); the F1
  zero-spawn-when-idle assertion still passes.
- If F2 concludes a `wl sync` perf fix is a separate work item, this item stays
  limited to pane-side isolation and references that item — no scope creep.

## Minimal Implementation

- Route auto-sync through the same background-task runtime used elsewhere
  (`packages/herdr/src` background helpers) with explicit event-loop decoupling
  and a tiny status model the pane renders without blocking.
- Add in-flight instrumentation (process start + PID + elapsed) so a refresh
  can verify non-interference; extend F1 harness with a "sync in flight"
  scenario.
- Add the non-blocking status notice and back it with the automated
  responsiveness test above.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — spawn path, single-flight, heartbeat.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — refresh orchestration + status rendering.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — in-flight sync scenario.

## Deliverables

- Off-loop auto-sync with status notice, in-flight instrumentation, an
  automated responsiveness-under-sync test, and updated
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` notes.

## Dependencies

- F2 profile results (plus F1 harness).

# F4 — In-process dependency and child reads on expand

## Background

Expanding a node still triggers per-item `wl dep list` (hydrator, ≈ 0.4 s each)
and single-parent `wl list --parent` spawns (`fetchChildrenForItem`); each
spawn costs 0.5–0.9 s and ~130–145 MB RSS. The batching in-process path already
exists for multi-parent fetches (`fetchChildrenForItems` via the refresh
scope) but the single-parent and per-hydrator-item paths still spawn. Parent
AC 2 bounds refresh end-to-end to ≤ ~1.5 s including per-expand child fetches,
and AC 5 bounds aggregate spawn RSS.

## Target outcome

Expanding a node (or hydrating its deps) performs zero `wl` spawns on the
large-DB path: all child/dependency reads are served in-process through the
one refresh-scoped SQLite connection, with the existing fail-open CLI fallback
unchanged for correctness edge cases.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Expanding a parent performs no `wl list --parent` / `wl dep list` spawn (F1
  spawn-count assertion) when the in-process path is available; child and
  dependency rows match the CLI's ordering, fields, depth and enrichment
  semantics on a ~2,600-item fixture.
- Hydrator dependency lookups use the in-process/refresh-scope read (or a
  bounded batched lookup) instead of one `wl dep list` spawn per item; the
  hydrator timeout behaviour from WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P is preserved.
- Fail-open preserved: when no worklog dir / SQLite file / `@worklog/shared` is
  available, or a stored audit fingerprint requires CLI enrichment, behaviour
  falls back to spawns exactly as today (existing `fetcher-inprocess` and
  `worklist-expand-refresh` tests still green).
- The one-open-per-refresh scope is kept — no new per-helper DB opens are
  introduced (parent AC constraints).
- Existing Herdr + TUI suites pass with zero-spawn-when-idle preserved (parent
  AC 6).

## Minimal Implementation

- Route `fetchChildrenForItem` through the shared batch/in-process reader when
  a scope is available; keep its signature and fail-open.
- Convert per-item hydrator `wl dep list` calls to a batched in-process dep
  read within the refresh scope (grouping visible items into one pass), with
  fail-open for the fingerprint/enrichment cases.
- Extend F1 harness assertions (expanded-node spawn counts) and the
  `fetchChildrenForItem/ForItems` in-process tests.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — single-parent fetch + batch reader + scope.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — per-item `wl dep list` calls.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — expand orchestration.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-inprocess.test.ts`, `worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts` — extend.

## Deliverables

- Spawn-free expand + hydrator dep reads on the in-process path, updated
  fail-open tests, F1 harness assertions green, and a completion comment with
  large-DB timing/spawn deltas vs baseline.

## Dependencies

- F2 profile results (confirms dep/child reads as a cost driver) and F1
  harness baselines.

# F5 — Bound `wl` spawn memory and concurrency for a single pane

## Background

Each surviving `wl worklist`/`wl list` spawn peaks at ~130–145 MB RSS on a
~100 MB DB (intake measurements). Parent AC 5 is satisfied either by reducing
per-spawn memory below a documented budget or by bounding concurrent spawns so
aggregate RSS for a single pane stays under a documented ceiling (e.g.
≤ ~300 MB). F2 determines where the memory goes and whether the `wl worklist`
payload can be trimmed without breaking its documented contract.

## Target outcome

A documented, enforced per-pane RSS/spawn budget that guarantees parent AC 5
at large-DB scale, without regressing small-DB behaviour or the consolidated
single-read default view.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-spawn or aggregate budget confirmed: measured peak aggregate RSS for a
  single pane during a full refresh (F1 harness, full scale) is at or below a
  documented ceiling (target ≤ ~300 MB as in parent AC 5), OR per-spawn peak is
  reduced below the ~130–145 MB observed baseline and the reduced number is
  documented as the new budget.
- Based on F2's evidence, either: (a) a payload trim on `wl worklist` (drop
  unused fields/streaming) with the documented payload contract preserved or
  explicitly revised and tested, or (b) a documented spawn cap (e.g. N
  concurrent `wl` spawns, queueing/deferred reads) whose aggregate RSS is
  asserted by an automated test — without waiting under the event loop.
- The budget and its enforcement are documented in
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` (parent AC 5 "documented budget").
- No regression to small worklogs and no change to the consolidated
  single-read default-view norm; zero-spawn-when-idle preserved (parent AC 6).
- All remaining `wl` spawns execute off the TUI event loop, and deferred/
  queued reads never block input: the F1 harness event-loop aggregation stays
  within the parent AC 1 ≤ ~200 ms bound with a spawn-heavy fixture (intake
  candidate 4).
- No new heavy dependencies (parent constraints) — prefer reuse of the
  in-process SQLite read path over new spawns.

## Minimal Implementation

- Apply the F2-validated memory fix (payload trim with contract test, or
  streaming) and/or add a concurrency semaphore around `wl` spawns in the
  fetch path with queued fallback reads.
- Add F1 harness assertions for aggregate RSS, spawn count, and event-loop
  blocking at full scale.
- Ensure every remaining spawn is dispatched off the TUI event loop (existing
  background-task runtime) with a bounded queue; assert no input-lock via the
  harness.
- Update docs; record before/after numbers in the completion comment.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — spawn path, exec seam, spawn cap.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — payload build (if trim chosen).
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — RSS/spawn assertions.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — budget documentation.

## Deliverables

- Enforced spawn/RSS budget with automated assertion, validated memory fix
  (trim or cap) per F2 evidence, docs, and measured before/after numbers.

## Dependencies

- F2 (memory breakdown + payload-contract decision), F1 harness.

# F6 — Single, cheap in-process SQLite open per refresh

## Background

In-process SQLite reads on a ~100 MB DB carry a non-trivial open cost (open +
pragmas + FTS DDL ~46–70 ms measured in earlier work; the one-open-per-refresh
scope from WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B exists to amortise it). Surviving per-helper
opens, read-only open DDL, and connection reuse across ticks are the remaining
levers. Parent AC 2 (≤ ~1.5 s default-view refresh p95) and AC 1 (no event-loop
stall) constrain this cost; F2 quantifies its share.

## Target outcome

A default-view refresh performs at most one cheap in-process SQLite open
(shared across all refresh helpers, read-only, minimal/no DDL when already
initialised), and the open cost is small enough that it never threatens the
refresh budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An automated test (F1 harness, full scale) asserts a default-view refresh
  performs at most one in-process DB open per refresh and that helper reads
  reuse that single connection (no per-helper open).
- The read-only open path is measured and documented: open+pragmas cost is
  recorded after the change (target: eliminate the ~46–70 ms FTS-DDL hit on
  already-initialised stores, e.g. by skipping DDL when schema/version already
  present), with numbers below the refresh budget headroom.
- Open is verified off the TUI event loop / within the existing refresh scope
  (parent AC 1); any background warm-up does not overlap a visible refresh in a
  blocking way.
- Fail-open preserved: a read-only open failure degrades to the existing `wl`
  spawn fallback; no change to the hydrator's core behaviour or scheduler
  (parent constraints).
- Existing Herdr + TUI suites pass; zero-spawn-when-idle preserved (parent
  AC 6).

## Minimal Implementation

- Refactor the refresh-scope open to: one shared connection per refresh across
  all helpers, read-only pragma set, and schema/DDL only when required
  (version check); verify `@worklog/shared` `WorklogDatabase` surface honours
  a read-only/no-DDL mode or the skip is done at the caller.
- Add harness timing for the open step; update docs budgeting the open cost.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — refresh scope + `InProcessRefreshScope` open.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `WorklogDatabase` open/DDL path.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — open-cost timing.

## Deliverables

- One-cheap-open-per-refresh with automated single-open + timing assertions,
  fail-open tests green, and documented open-cost numbers.

## Dependencies

- F2 (quantifies open cost share), F1 harness.

# F7 — Large-DB responsiveness verification at scale

## Background

The parent's ACs are acceptance criteria for the whole pane behaviour at scale.
F1–F6 each deliver targeted fixes and tests; this item is the end-to-end
verification slice that confirms every parent AC holds together on a
~2,600-item / ~100 MB fixture after all changes, including the AC 4
write→reflect re-verification (extending WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN to large-DB
scale) and AC 6's full-suite no-regression gate.

## Target outcome

One reproducible end-to-end evidence run (documented commands + test suite)
that every parent acceptance criterion 1–6 is met at large-DB scale.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pane stays responsive during refresh:** a default-view refresh does not block the TUI event loop for more than ~200 ms of perceived lag in aggregate (verified with an automated test harness or measured timing on a large fixture DB) — keystrokes/commands process promptly while a refresh is in flight. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Single-figure refresh cost on large DBs:** a default-view refresh end-to-end (event → data load → render) is bounded to ≤ ~1.5 s wall-clock p95 on a DB of ~2,600 items / ~100 MB, including per-expand child fetches; the consolidated `wl worklist` single-read path stays the norm — no regression to multi-spawn refreshes. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Auto-sync cannot stall the pane:** while a long `wl sync` (measured ~36 s on the 100 MB DB) is in flight in the background, the pane remains responsive — no lock wait, no event-loop stall, at most a brief non-blocking status notice. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Change reflection latency:** after a `wl` write, the pane reflects the change within ~2 s p95 via the event-driven watch path at large-DB scale. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Reduced memory footprint:** a refresh's spawned `wl` processes peak at no more than a documented per-spawn budget below the ~130–145 MB/spawn observed baseline, OR concurrent spawns are bounded so aggregate RSS for a single pane stays under a documented ceiling (e.g. ≤ ~300 MB). (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **No regressions:** the full Herdr plugin + TUI test suites pass; the zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee and event-driven watch semantics are preserved. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)

- All measured numbers are quoted in the completion comment against the F1 baseline; if any criterion is not met, the blocking fix item is referenced with its data rather than accepted silently.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the F1 harness with an end-to-end "all ACs" report mode aggregating
  every metric into one JSON report plus a human summary.
- Drive the event-driven write→reflect measurement at full scale (reusing the
  watch path from WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN) and assert AC 4 at large-DB scale.
- Run the full suite + full-scale harness, record the report comment, and mark
  this item (and via parent workflow, the parent) ready once green.

# Impl: change-detection persist in db.import / db.importComments

## Background

F2 (WL-0MVJV2NNG00771C6) measured the sync persist phase at 83.6 s of an 85.9 s pipeline on the 123.7 MB fixture, with 78–90 % of the CPU inside `upsertFtsEntry`. `db.import()` clears every work item, re-saves every item and then re-indexes the FTS row of every item; `db.importComments()` clears every comment, re-saves every comment and re-indexes the FTS row of every item. A no-change sync therefore pays the whole cost. This item implements the fix behind parent ACs 1, 3 and 4.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `db.import()` writes only records whose merged value differs from the local store: unchanged work items/edges/audits are not re-saved, while `updatedAt` preservation and the later-`activityAt` merge still hold (an otherwise identical item carrying a later incoming `activityAt` is still persisted so no activity timestamp is lost).
- Records absent from the incoming full snapshot are still deleted (work items, comments, edges) and only those deleted ids have their FTS rows removed — `clearWorkItems()`/`clearComments()` no longer force a full FTS rebuild, with existing callers (`importData()`, `doctor migrate`, `clear()`) keeping their current destructive behaviour.
- `db.importComments()` writes only changed/new comments and performs FTS upkeep only for the affected parent item ids — FTS maintenance is proportional to changed items, never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge (the delta `upsertComments()` path too: look up only the affected ids instead of scanning every item).
- Each record type is persisted inside one transaction (or batched statements): `db.importComments()` gains a transaction wrapping its clear/save/FTS work, no per-row transaction is introduced, and `db.import()`'s existing atomicity is preserved.
- Existing sync contracts still hold — delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results — and the existing sync and FTS tests plus the write-detection tests from the verification item stay green.

- Change detection: only records whose merged value differs from the local store are written (`saveWorkItem`/`saveComment`/edges/audits); a no-change sync performs zero writes and zero FTS writes.
- FTS maintenance is proportional to CHANGED items (per-changed-item `upsertFtsEntry` or one batched/transactional re-index), never a full re-index of all items after a comment merge.
- Records are persisted in one transaction (or batched statements) per record type — no per-row transaction — and the existing sync contracts still hold: delta push/fallback/convergence, watermark advance only after a successful push, divergence → full snapshot, FTS search results. Existing sync and FTS tests stay green.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `import()`, `importComments()`, `upsertItems()`, `upsertComments()`, `hasWorkItemChanged`/`compareTrackedFields`, `mergeAuditsNewestWins`.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `upsertFtsEntry`, `clearWorkItems`, `clearComments`, `saveComment`, `saveWorkItem`, `transaction`.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `performSync` persist branch (delta via `upsertItems`/`upsertComments`, full snapshot via `import`/`importComments`).

## Dependencies

- Verify item (persist write-detection regression tests) — test-first.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `import()`: compute the diff against the existing snapshot — unchanged records (per `hasWorkItemChanged`) are skipped entirely (no `saveWorkItem`), changed/new records are saved, ids absent from the incoming set are deleted with only their FTS rows removed; keep the transaction and `updatedAt`/`activityAt` semantics.
- In `importComments()`: diff comments by identity fields, skip unchanged saves, delete removed comments, wrap clear/save/FTS in one transaction, and re-index FTS only for the affected parent ids.
- Reduce `upsertComments()` to look up only the affected parent ids (no full table scan) and confirm no full FTS rebuild remains after a comment merge.
- Preserve `clearWorkItems()`/`clearComments()` for their remaining callers; introduce targeted FTS-row deletion for the sync path.

## Deliverables

- Rewritten persist path: writes and FTS work proportional to actually-changed records, transactions per record type, contracts unchanged.
data.title: Impl: change-detection persist in db.import / db.importComments

## Problem

The downtime dispatcher's no-dispatch decision log (`<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`) is capped at **100 lines** (rolling). On a busy machine that is roughly **one hour** of history, because every tick that is refused for a capacity/prefill reason writes a decision entry.

During the 2026-10-22/23 overnight starvation investigation this meant the whole night could not be reconstructed: the retained window started at `2026-10-23T05:59:58Z` and the decisions for the preceding ~8 hours had already been rotated out. The pre-05:30 reasons had to be *inferred* from pi session activity instead of read from the log.

For contrast, the retained 84-minute window carried 66 no-dispatch decisions — so the cap is genuinely exhausted in about an hour of saturated polling.

## Why it matters

- Capacity-saturation starvation is silent by design (NOP), so the decision log is the **only** forensic evidence that dispatch was attempted and why it was refused.
- Post-mortem of an overnight outage ("why did almost nothing dispatch?") is currently impossible after the fact; the operator has to guess.
- The same problem affects distinguishing `capacity-saturated` / `slots-unavailable` / `prefill-cap` / `idle-age-pending` / `no-candidate` / `review-queue-hold` / `code-freeze` after rotation.

## Goal

As an operator, I want at least a full night (24 h) of downtime dispatch decisions to remain available on a busy machine, so that a post-mortem can report the actual terminal reasons and their counts, with bounded disk use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — On a machine producing decision entries at the observed rate (≥ 60/hour), at least the **last 24 hours** of `no-dispatch` decisions are readable after the fact (verified by a test that writes > 1,500 entries and asserts the oldest 24 h window is still present).
- [ ] AC2 — Disk growth is bounded: rotation happens on a documented size/time policy (e.g. daily files with a retention window, or size-based rotation with N kept), and the policy is configurable with a documented default.
- [ ] AC3 — An operator-facing, documented way exists to reconstruct a time-range summary (e.g. `wl`/herdr command, or documented `grep`/`jq` recipe over rotated files) that prints a reason tally per hour for a given night.
- [ ] AC4 — Existing readers/parsers of the single `downtime-coordination.log` path are either migrated atomically or continue to read the newest file without change; no dispatch decision is lost across a rotation boundary (test asserted).
- [ ] AC5 — Docs updated: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` log-schema/observability section names the retention policy and the summary recipe.

## Evidence (2026-10-23 investigation)

- `ContextHub/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`: 100 entries covering `2026-10-23T05:59:58.509Z` → `2026-10-23T07:13:27.061Z`.
- Reason tally in that retained window: `capacity-saturated` 29, `slots-unavailable` 29, `idle-age-pending` 4, `prefill-cap` 2, `idle-age-qualified` 2 (66 no-dispatch decisions).
- Earlier overnight window (roughly `2026-10-22T21:00Z` → `2026-10-23T05:30Z`) had no retained decision records at all.

## Notes

- Related: the starvation investigation item covering long-running panes holding local-LLM capacity.
- No production behaviour change to dispatch decisions is in scope — this is observability only.
data.title: herdr: retain 24h of downtime dispatcher decision history (coordination log rotates in ~1h)

# Finalise downtime-worker barrel and docs

**Parent:** WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — decompose `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
**Scope:** the residual `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` content (module doc comment + import/export wiring) plus the documentation updates and the final verification pass for the epic.

## Goal

As a consumer of the downtime worker, I want `downtime-worker.ts` to be a thin,
honest barrel that re-exports exactly the symbols other modules actually use, and
I want the dispatcher docs to show the module layout, so that the public surface
is discoverable and the epic's acceptance criteria are verifiable in one pass.

## Scope

- Reduce `downtime-worker.ts` to: module-level doc comment (kept provenance,
  trimmed to a short overview + pointer to the module layout), and
  `export … from './downtime-worker.*.js'` statements only.
- Re-export **only symbols actually imported by consumers** (134 baseline symbols
  captured by the split-guard child); stop re-exporting symbols no consumer and
  no sibling module uses.
- Empty `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` in `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` so the size
  gate now covers every `downtime-worker*.ts` module including the barrel.
- Documentation: add a "Module layout" section to
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (module → single responsibility → key
  exports), update `packages/herdr/README.md` if it names internals, and fix any
  code comments that still describe the monolith.
- Record the final verification evidence on the epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wc -l packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` ≤ 250, and the file contains no
   function/type/const declarations — only the doc comment and re-exports.
2. The barrel re-exports exactly the 134 consumer-imported symbols from the
   baseline, and no symbol that neither a consumer nor a sibling module imports;
   a scan comparing barrel exports against the baseline (plus sibling-module
   imports) is recorded as evidence.
3. `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` is empty and the split-guard test proves every
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.ts` production module (including the
   barrel) is ≤1,000 lines; the allowlist-shrink assertion is satisfied.
4. The split-guard public-surface, single-flight, cycle and size gates all pass;
   the import graph has no cycle beyond the recorded pre-existing type-only
   `stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker` cycle, and no split module imports the
   barrel at runtime.
5. The 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite
   pass **unmodified**, and the full repo suite passes (`/skill:test` full).
6. `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` contains a "Module layout" section listing
   every module created by the split with its single responsibility, and no doc
   or comment still refers to `downtime-worker.ts` as a 9,000-line monolith; a
   search of the repository docs, `docs/` site sources and the project wiki
   confirms no other page documents the old internal layout (result recorded in
   the evidence comment).
7. The build is green (`npm run build` / `npm run build:shared` as applicable)
   and `tsc` reports no new errors.
8. A comment on this item records: `wc -l` output for every module, the guard
   test output, the suite result, and the symbol → module mapping — enough to
   audit epic AC1–AC8 without re-running anything.
9. Every epic AC (1–8) is verified with the evidence above; any AC that cannot
   be met is raised as an OPEN QUESTION on the epic instead of being silently
   waived.

## Minimal implementation

1. Delete the remaining moved code from `downtime-worker.ts`; build the barrel
   export list from the baseline JSON (and sibling-module imports) so it is
   exactly the used surface.
2. Empty `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST`; run the guard suite and inspect each gate's output.
3. Rewrite the module doc comment: short overview, the ranking contract
   (Herdr list head is the sole ranking path), fail-closed note, and a pointer to
   the module layout table in the docs.
4. Add the docs module-layout section; update `packages/herdr/README.md` if it
   references internals.
5. Run `/skill:test` (full) + build; record the evidence comment; verify AC1–AC8.
6. Verify moved blocks match the pre-split source (`git show <pre-split>:...`
   diff review) and note the result.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — becomes the thin barrel
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` — allowlist emptied
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — module layout section
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — internal references, if any
- all `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.ts` — read-only verification

## Dependencies

Blocked by: orchestrator child. Final child of the epic.

## Notes

This child is the only one permitted to change the barrel's exported symbol set
(Q2 refinement). Removing an unused re-export is intended — but a symbol that a
test file imports is *used* and must stay, because test files may not be
modified (parent AC3).

## Summary

Add a `wl doctor prefix` subcommand that changes the configured project prefix in `.worklog/config.yaml` and renumbers every existing work item to the new prefix, preserving each item's suffix (e.g. `OSL-0MVK31VYQ007CN37` → `CC-0MVK31VYQ007CN37`). The flow must ask for confirmation before it changes anything, default to a read-only preview, and emit a machine-readable rename map.

## Motivation

Requested from the ContentCreator project (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator`), whose configured prefix is `OSL` while the project is now branded `CC`. 1207 work items carry the `OSL-` prefix, and `wl doctor foreign-items` correctly classifies any item whose prefix differs from `.worklog/config.yaml` as foreign — so editing the prefix by hand would make the whole backlog look foreign and break cross-project lookups.

## Scope (proposed)

- `wl doctor prefix` — read-only preview: current prefix, counts of items/comments/dependency edges/audit records, and sample renames.
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX>` — declare the target prefix (validated: non-empty, no `-`, ASCII alphanumeric).
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX> --confirm` — apply: rewrite the config prefix, then rewrite every ID-bearing record (`workitems.id`, parent references, dependency edges, comments' `workItemId`, audit results, waivers, and any other ID column), and write a rename map (`osl→cc` pairs) to `.worklog/prefix-rename-<timestamp>.json`.
- Confirmation gate: interactive run without `--confirm` prompts and requires an explicit `y`; a non-TTY run without `--confirm` aborts with no writes and a non-zero exit.
- Idempotent: re-running after a successful rename reports a no-op.
- `--json` output for scripting.
- Docs: `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` and `CLI.md`.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- [ ] `wl doctor prefix` (preview) reports counts and sample renames and changes nothing; covered by unit and temp-store integration tests.
- [ ] `--confirm` rewrites every ID-bearing record (items, parents, dependency edges, comments, audit results, waivers) and writes the rename map.
- [ ] Confirmation gate: non-interactive without `--confirm` aborts with a non-zero exit and zero writes; interactive requires explicit `y`.
- [ ] Re-running after a successful rename is a no-op, and a mid-run failure leaves the store recoverable (transactional or a documented rollback).
- [ ] `wl doctor foreign-items` reports zero foreign items after a confirmed rename.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated (CLI.md, DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md, code comments).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Out of scope

Rewriting ID references held outside the worklog store — code comments, docs, test fixtures, git commit messages, branch and worktree names. The requesting project owns that sweep and will use the rename map.

## Related

- Requested by work in the ContentCreator project (`discovered-from` recorded there).

## Summary

`.worklog/config.defaults.yaml` in this repo has no `syncAllowedAuthors` list, so `wl sync` runs the author-identity gate in strict mode: it refuses to merge any incoming commit on `refs/worklog/data` whose author email differs from the store's `git config user.email`. The shared ref carries 3,687 commits authored by `pi@local` while this checkout's `user.email` is `sorra@thewizardscode.com`, so agent-initiated `wl sync` runs here were refused and needed `--allow-foreign-author`.

## Fix (as shipped)

Declare a narrow allow-list in `.worklog/config.yaml` — **not** in `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml`: that file is this repository's project *template* (`projectName: TestProject`, `prefix: TEST`), so identities listed there would leak into every project created from it.

```yaml
syncAllowedAuthors:
  - 250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com
  - pi@local
```

Never use `null`/`true` (allow-all); empty-author commits must stay refused.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The effective `syncAllowedAuthors` (defaults merged with `.worklog/config.yaml`) lists both identities, and `config.yaml` never shadows a defaults entry with a narrower list.
- [x] `wl sync` and `wl sync --dry-run` succeed in this checkout without `--allow-foreign-author`.
- [x] A guard test drives the real config merge and the real gate: listed authors accepted, unknown author refused, empty author refused even with the allow-all override (`tests/config-sync-allowed-authors.test.ts`).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes — blocked by `tests/unit/persist-write-detection.test.ts`, already red on `dev` before this change (9 failures, introduced by commit `0d8324df`); triaged as `WL-0MVM9E3SV003III0`.

## Observed

Found while filing WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J (prefix rename request) on 2026-10-24; the first sync was completed with `--allow-foreign-author` as a one-off, then `git pull` was run and `wl sync` re-tested.

# If Critical item is a child it should not show in top level herdr selection list (WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI)

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist renders critical-priority work items that have a `parentId` at the **top level** of the selection list, even when their parent is also listed — so a critical child appears twice: once as a standalone top-level row and once under its parent when expanded. The top level should contain only root items; a critical child must appear only as a child.

Confirmed live reproduction: `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY` (critical, blocked, `intake_complete`, parent `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0`) is a child of `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0` (critical, in-progress). Both render at top level.

## Users

- **Producer / operator using the Herdr worklist** — browses the top-level selection list to choose what to work on next.
  - *As a producer, I want the top-level list to contain only root work items, so I am not shown the same unit of work twice and the list stays short enough to scan.*
- **Developer/agent triaging critical work** — needs release-blocking critical work to remain discoverable.
  - *As a triager, I want a critical child to be reachable from the top level via its parent, so hiding the duplicate row does not make the work invisible.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Top-level invariant**: the default Herdr worklist contains **no** item with a non-empty `parentId`, critical items included. Enforced on the merged set (browse feed + all mandatory subsets) for **both** fetch paths — the consolidated `wl worklist` bundle path (`assembleDefaultWorklist`) and the per-subset fallback — and by removing the `|| i.priority === 'critical'` exception from the root filter in `selectWorkItems`.
2. **Parent substitution preserves reachability**: when a critical child is dropped from the top level, its **root ancestor** (walking the `parentId` chain to the top-most non-child item) is included instead whenever that root is not already in the selected set. The substituted root joins the mandatory set (always shown, not subject to `browseItemCount`) and is sorted by its own priority/group. No badge, marker, or indicator is added to the substituted row.
3. **No regression for existing behaviour**:
   - non-critical children remain hidden from the top level exactly as today;
   - drill-down/expand still returns children unchanged (`fetchChildrenForItem` / `fetchChildrenForItems`, including critical children);
   - stage-filtered and priority-filtered views remain strictly root-only filters with **no** synthetic/substituted rows;
   - the CLI is unchanged for other consumers: `wl list --priority critical` still returns children (the ship critical-items gate must keep seeing them) and `wl worklist`'s `critical` subset keeps its current all-parent-levels query.
4. **Testing & validation**: unit tests cover the removed critical exception, the substitution rule (root ancestor promotion, parent already visible → no duplicate, parent in a non-critical group, count/mandatory interaction), and both fetch paths; the previously added critical-exception tests are updated/inverted. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.
5. **Documentation**: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. At minimum: the root-filter comment in `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`, the critical-subset note in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` and `src/commands/worklist.ts`, and the Herdr worklist section of `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Constraints

- **No new hot-path `wl` spawn.** Root-ancestor resolution must use the existing in-process SQLite fast path first (`withInProcessDb` / refresh scope `db.get`), with `wl show` only as a fail-open fallback. The refresh-spawn budget work (WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78, WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG) must not regress.
- **No data mutation.** Substitution is display-layer only: never rewrite the parent's stored `priority`, `status`, or `stage`.
- **Keep the `wl worklist` critical subset query as-is** (all parent levels, one spawn). It doubles as the discovery feed that tells the Herdr layer which parents to surface; making it root-only would require a second query per refresh.
- **Ship-gate semantics untouched.** `wl list --priority critical --status open` (exit code 7 gate) and the downtime critical candidate path keep their current child-inclusive behaviour.
- Fail-open: if a parent cannot be resolved (missing/deleted), the child is simply not shown at top level — never crash the refresh, never fall back to rendering the child at top level.

## Existing state

- **Why the duplicate exists today.** Commit `cae8ea8a` ("fix: show child critical items in worklist selection list") deliberately reintroduced critical children into the top level: the critical subset query dropped `--root-only` and `selectWorkItems` gained the `|| i.priority === 'critical'` root-filter exception. Rationale: child criticals (e.g. untriaged `[test-failure]` items) were invisible in the worklist while the ship critical-items gate still blocked release on them (exit code 7).
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems` root filter: `items.filter((i) => !i.parentId || i.priority === 'critical')`; `isMandatoryItem` treats any critical item as mandatory.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — `WORKLIST_LIST_SUBSET_QUERIES.critical = { priority: 'critical', status: ['open','in-progress','blocked','completed'] }` with **no** `rootOnly`, documented as "all parent levels: a critical child is as urgent as a critical root". `reviewQueue`, `inProgressRoots`, `blockedRoots` are all `rootOnly: true`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchMandatorySubsets` issues `wl list --priority critical --status open,in-progress,blocked,completed` (no `--root-only`); `assembleDefaultWorklist` merges bundle subsets with the browse feed then calls `selectWorkItems` + `regroupWorkItems`; the per-subset fallback mirrors this. `fetchItemsByStage` / `fetchItemsByPriority` already pass `--root-only`.
- `wl worklist` is consumed only by `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (verified by search), so its payload shape is effectively a Herdr-internal contract.
- Current data: 174 critical items, 78 of them children — 77 of those are themselves `completed`/`done` (already filtered by the `stage !== 'done'` rule in `selectWorkItems`), leaving **one** live duplicate: `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY`.
- The Pi TUI Worklog extension has no critical-subset or smart-selection code (removed by WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N), so no Pi-side change is needed.
- Parent rows already carry `childCount` (rendered as a `Children: N` metadata row and an expand icon), so a substituted parent is discoverable as a container.

## Desired change

1. **`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`** — root filter becomes `items.filter((i) => !i.parentId)` (no critical exception). Update the doc comment to state the invariant and the substitution contract.
2. **`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`** — add a display-layer substitution step shared by `assembleDefaultWorklist` and the per-subset fallback:
   - partition the critical subset into root criticals (kept) and critical children (dropped from the top level);
   - for each critical child, resolve its root ancestor by walking `parentId` upward;
   - for each resolved root not already present in the merged candidate set, add it to the **mandatory** set (so `browseItemCount` cannot cut it) before `selectWorkItems` runs;
   - resolve parents in-process first (`db.get` via the refresh scope / `withInProcessDb`), falling back to `wl show`; unresolvable parents are skipped (fail-open).
3. **`src/commands/worklist.ts`** — documentation-only update: state that the `critical` subset is intentionally all-parent-levels (discovery feed) and that the top-level-only invariant is enforced by the Herdr consumer.
4. **Tests** — invert/extend `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts` (child critical hidden; non-critical children still hidden) and add fetcher-level coverage for both paths in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` plus the per-subset fallback tests.
5. **Docs** — update `packages/herdr/README.md` (worklist/selection behaviour) and the affected code comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — remove the critical exception from the root filter; document the invariant and substitution contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `assembleDefaultWorklist` + per-subset fallback: critical-child partition, root-ancestor resolution, mandatory-set injection; in-process-first parent lookup with `wl show` fail-open fallback.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts` — invert the "shows child critical items at the top level" case; keep/extend non-critical child cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` — bundle path: child critical not rendered at top level; parent substituted and mandatory.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.test.ts` (per-subset fallback coverage, whichever file currently exercises `fetchNextItems` without the bundle) — same assertions on the fallback path.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — comment/documentation update for the `critical` subset (no behaviour change).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — selection-list behaviour documentation.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** — *Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr)* (completed). Introduced the root-only invariant; its critical-related behaviour was later superseded by commit `cae8ea8a`. This item restores the invariant for critical items while keeping reachability via parent substitution.
- **commit `cae8ea8a`** — "fix: show child critical items in worklist selection list" (no work-item reference in the commit message): the deliberate exception this item reverses. Its motivation — critical children flagged by the ship gate being invisible — is preserved through AC2.
- **WL-0MQFIYPZK00680H1** — *wl next should return parent items instead of surfacing children individually* (completed): precedent for "represented by parent".
- **WL-0MQI1SX4W0018V9O** — *Child work items appear in Pi TUI selection list when they should be hidden (represented by parent)* (completed): same precedent, Pi side.
- **WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B** — *Selection list must always show all completed/in_review and critical items regardless of browseItemCount* (completed): defines the mandatory subsets whose "always shown" rule AC2 preserves for substituted parents.
- **WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C** — *Bubble up critical items* (completed): created the dedicated "Critical" group that sits first in the grouped output. Relevant because a substituted parent is **not** critical by priority, so it will not land in that group (see Risks).
- **WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR** — *Auto-downgrade critical children when parent priority is reduced* (completed): related priority-inheritance behaviour for critical children.
- **WL-0MV6KV22S004NYIU / WL-0MV71WBHB007D8ZE** — mandatory in-progress-root and blocked-root subsets: the sibling subsets that already use `--root-only`.
- **WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78 / WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG** — spawn-budget work governing the consolidated `wl worklist` read and in-process refresh scope that the substitution must reuse.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Lost top-level visibility (accepted, mitigated).** Hiding critical children means an operator scanning only the top level no longer sees them directly; the ship critical-items gate can still block a release on a child. Mitigation: AC2 surfaces the root ancestor so the work stays reachable; the parent must be expanded to see the child itself.
- **Substituted parent is not marked critical** (operator decision Q3 = no indicator). It joins the mandatory set and is sorted by its own priority/group, so it may sit in a non-critical section. Risk: the release-blocking signal is less prominent. Accepted; revisit as a separate item if it proves insufficient.
- **Parent resolution cost.** Only critical children trigger a lookup, and only when the root is absent from the merged set (currently one such item). In-process read first; `wl show` is the rare fallback. A per-refresh memo should avoid repeat lookups within a tick.
- **Ancestor promotion depth.** A critical grandchild promotes its **top-most** ancestor, keeping the "no child at top level" invariant. Assumption: promoting the root (not the immediate parent) is correct because the top level may only contain roots.
- **Stage/priority-filtered views are exempt from substitution.** They are explicit filters ("every open item in this stage") and already root-only; injecting a synthetic parent row would misrepresent the filter. Accepted assumption: the ship-gate reachability requirement applies to the default worklist.
- **`wl worklist` payload keeps children in the `critical` subset.** Documented as the discovery feed; a future consumer reading the payload directly would still see children. Accepted, documented in `src/commands/worklist.ts`.
- **Scope creep.** No changes to grouping rules, detail views, badges, or the Pi TUI. Any follow-up (e.g. a critical-child indicator on parents) becomes a separate work item.
- **Assumption**: `parentId` is always present in the payloads used (`wl list`, `wl next`, `wl worklist`) — already relied upon by the existing root-only filters.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** – Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr) (completed)
- **WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C** – Bubble up critical items (completed)
- **WL-0MQP4RDG2006LFM9** – Fix ruff lint findings in tests/test_audit_runner_core.py (completed) — *keyword-only match, unrelated*

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: another, appear, child, children, critical, extension, herdr, level, list, selection, should, show, they, top
- `CLI.md` — matched: same keywords
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: same keywords

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1** (intake round 1): "What should happen to a critical child whose parent is *not* otherwise in the top-level list (e.g. parent is `done`, or filtered out by the current stage/priority view)? (a) hide it entirely, (b) substitute the parent — show the parent row instead, (c) fallback exception — hide when the parent is visible, show the child when the parent is not, (d) freeform." — **Answer (user, interactive reply): "1. B"** — substitute the parent; the child is never rendered at top level.
- **Q2** (intake round 1): "Which lists should the fix cover? (a) default Herdr worklist only, (b) all Herdr top-level lists — default worklist, stage-filtered, priority-filtered, plus both fetch paths, (c) (b) plus CLI semantics, (d) freeform." — **Answer (user, interactive reply): "2. B"** — all Herdr top-level lists and both fetch paths; CLI `wl list`/ship-gate semantics unchanged.
- **Q3** (intake round 1): "Should a parent row show a 'critical child' indicator (badge/count) when it is surfaced because of a critical child?" — **Answer (user, interactive reply): "3. no"** — no indicator.
- **Derived assumptions (no question asked)**: (i) a critical child promotes its **top-most** ancestor, because the top level may only contain roots; (ii) stage/priority-filtered views get no substitution — they are explicit filters and already root-only; (iii) the substituted parent keeps its own priority/group (no critical marking, per Q3); (iv) an unresolvable parent means the child is simply not shown (fail-open).
- **Research note**: verified via `wl worklist --json` that the `critical` subset is the only mandatory subset without `rootOnly` (174 items, 78 children; 77 of those are `completed`/`done` and already filtered by the `stage !== 'done'` rule, leaving one live duplicate `WL-0MVSNHCSM004JYEY` under `WL-0MVSI1JMN002CGC0`). Traced the deliberate exception to commit `cae8ea8a` (no work-item reference) which removed `--root-only` from the critical query and added the `priority === 'critical'` root-filter exception to keep ship-gate-flagged child criticals visible. Confirmed `wl worklist` has a single consumer (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) and that `fetchItemsByStage`/`fetchItemsByPriority` already pass `--root-only`. Confirmed the Pi TUI has no critical-subset/smart-selection code.

# Split worklist TUI loop into context and handlers

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B. **Phase:** 6 of 7 (the hard part).

## Target outcome

`runWorklistTui` (currently lines 5581–7899, ~2,319 lines of nested closures over
one mutable context) becomes a thin orchestrator over named handler modules,
with a **single interface-typed context object owned by one module** and passed
explicitly to handler functions — no state duplication and no class-based
controller rewrite (parent constraint).

## Scope (measured closure groups inside `runWorklistTui`)

| New module | Contents | Est. size |
|---|---|---|
| `worklist.tui-context.ts` | The context interface + factory: `opts`, `termSize`, `items`, `state`, `renderer`, `inputActive`, view flags (`formState`, `preFormMode`, `preHelpMode`, `helpScrollOffset`, `shipItDialog`, `podcastNotice`, `blockedNotice`), freeze/sprint flags, dispose hooks. Single owner of the mutable context (AC5) | ~250 |
| `worklist.tui-handlers.ts` | Pane gate, agent tracker, live event subscriptions, pane-marker apply/refresh/batching, metadata blocker resolution + cache (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8), freeze-state refresh, review-queue sprint state | ~560 |
| `worklist.tui-refresh.ts` | Non-blocking sync status notice (F3 — WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N), `cleanup`, `closeEventSubscriber`, `doRefresh` (single-flight + pending), `doSync`, `openShipItDialog` / `openShipItDialogGuarded` | ~480 |
| `worklist.tui-input.ts` | `dispatchMouse`, `handleKeyInput`, streaming stdin decode (`onData` + `KeypressDecoder`), `readKeyFile`/`writeKeyFile`, `buildHelpEntries`/`buildHelpIconLegend` | ~800 |
| `worklist.tui-render.ts` | `render`, `onResize`, `TaskScheduler` wiring, hydrator runner, resume poll, db-change watch, and the `runWorklistTui` orchestrator that constructs the context and registers handlers | ~570 |

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `runWorklistTui` is retained at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical
   signature and return type (`Promise<WorkItem | undefined>`), implemented as a
   thin orchestrator (context construction + handler registration + teardown);
   no module and no single exported function carries the former 2,319-line body
   (AC1).
2. Every new module ≤1,000 lines with a responsibility doc comment; the TUI-local
   sub-banners (metadata-panel dependency blockers — WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8,
   review-queue depth indicator, event-driven window status — WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ,
   non-blocking sync status notice — WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N, mouse event dispatch —
   WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ AC2–AC6, streaming stdin decode — WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH,
   consolidated scheduler loop — WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP, hydrator —
   WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI) and their inline work-item ids move verbatim (AC6).
3. **Single context, explicit passing.** The context type is declared once in
   `worklist.tui-context.ts`; handler modules receive it as a parameter and
   never re-declare a mutable field it already owns. `WorkItemListState`
   remains a single instance created by the orchestrator (AC5); the split guard's
   single-owner gate stays green.
4. Lifecycle ordering is preserved exactly: event-subscription setup, pane gate,
   refresh single-flight/pending, scheduler ticks, hydrator, resume poll and
   teardown order are unchanged — verified by the unmodified
   `worklist-integration.test.ts`, `worklist-active-pane-marker.test.ts`,
   `worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts`, `worklist-consolidated-refresh.test.ts`,
   `worklist-watch.test.ts`, `worklist-inflight.test.ts`,
   `worklist-sync-notice.test.ts` and `worklist.test.ts` TUI blocks (AC3).
5. Split guard, `tsc --noEmit`/build and the full `packages/herdr` suite pass;
   no new cycle; no runtime barrel import (AC4, AC9).
6. Docs updated: `packages/herdr/README.md` (module-layout block, `onPaneFocused`
   and `isInputActive` references at ~1619 and ~1781, and the ~1829 "task
   registration in `worklist.ts`" note), `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`,
   `docs/dev/herdr-events-subscribe-reliability.md`,
   `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`, `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md`,
   `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` — all path references resolve
   to the new modules.
7. **State ownership is explicit and singular.** The mutable
   `WorkItemListState` (848-line section) and the TUI-local mutable context
   currently closed over by `runWorklistTui` each live in exactly one module;
   extraction must not duplicate mutable state or fork the source of truth.
   → Owned by this slice: `WorkItemListState` and the extracted TUI context each live in exactly one module and no mutable state is duplicated.

## Minimal implementation

1. Introduce `worklist.tui-context.ts` with the context interface and factory;
   move the `opts`/state/flag declarations into it **without** changing any
   initial value or ordering.
2. Extract `worklist.tui-handlers.ts` (subscriptions, pane markers, blockers,
   freeze/sprint state) as functions taking the context.
3. Extract `worklist.tui-refresh.ts` (`doRefresh`/`doSync`/ship-it dialog/notice/
   cleanup) as functions taking the context.
4. Extract `worklist.tui-input.ts` (`handleKeyInput`/`dispatchMouse`/`onData`/
   key-file IO/help entries) as functions taking the context.
5. Extract `worklist.tui-render.ts` (render/resize/scheduler/hydrator/resume
   poll/db-change watch) and reduce `runWorklistTui` to orchestration.
   Land steps 1–5 as **separate commits**, each with the full suite green, so a
   behavioural regression is attributable to one closure group.
6. Run guard + build + suite; update docs.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-context.ts` — new (single context owner).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-handlers.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-refresh.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-input.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-render.ts` — new (holds the orchestrator).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — re-exports `runWorklistTui`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — consumer; must compile unchanged.
- Docs: `packages/herdr/README.md` and the five `docs/dev/*` files listed above.

## Constraints

- No class-based controller conversion, no state duplication, no reordering of
  lifecycle steps, no changed defaults or timings.
- The context is interface-typed and passed explicitly; closures may become
  module functions but must not change observable behaviour.
- No barrel/`index.ts` imports inside the new modules; no test edits.

## Dependencies

- `WL-0MVV3NB39001DG8J` — refactor guard (test-first).

- `WL-0MVND6F9V004IQ3V` — state/navigation.
- `WL-0MVND6H5Q006YO9Z` — presentation.
- `WL-0MVND6J090041GWK` — input pipeline (key/mouse handlers move with it).
- `WL-0MVND6KVF0089878` — renderer/commands (the loop dispatches through them).

## Deliverables

Five TUI modules with a thin `runWorklistTui`, guard + full suite green, docs
updated.

Producer finding from the machine-hygiene session (2025-10-21): propose_remediations() in skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py emits a renice action for every large RSS contributor under memory/swap pressure without inspecting the target's current nice value. In the observed run every proposed target was already at nice 19 or 0, and the targets included two live test suites (AI_Hell vitest, tce-the-rising browser suite) - the action would have slowed active work.

Suggested fix (from producer): skip renice when min(nice) over the target pids is already >= the proposed nice value, and surface the current nice value in the action's reason/target so the operator can see why an action is proposed or suppressed.

Note: this is deliberately separate from the duplication fix in WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ (dedupe + single render); this item is the semantic safety change and needs process-nice collection support.

Scope: scanning niceness (/proc/<pid>/stat field 19) for target pids, suppressing no-op renicces, and tests for both suppressed and emitted cases. Related: skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py (propose_remediations), metrics collection if nice must be collected centrally.

Goal: a local-only pane whose prompt exceeds the local provider's context ceiling should degrade predictably instead of stalling or failing, and the reason should be visible to the operator.

Observed problem: the local provider rejects a local-only request when the projected prompt exceeds ~38k tokens warm, or ~25k on a cold prefix. Because the pane is labelled local-only the proxy refuses the local route, and the work is not processed on the local slot. Evidence in this deployment's route logs (.worklog/local-route.log, 697 turns across 5 roots): 49 turns route remote with fallbackReason resident_prefix_insufficient and 44 with large_context_bypass; 72 turns actually served local. The thresholds and the exact refusal behaviour (hard error vs silent fallback) live in the external llama-proxy (LP project), not in this repo - confirm before designing the fix.

Open design questions to settle in plan:
- Is the correct behaviour a fallback to remote for over-threshold requests, an explicit hard error surfaced to the operator, or pre-dispatch routing (choose remote-ok when the projected context exceeds the ceiling)?
- Where is the projected context size knowable? The pi extension sees the outgoing request (before_provider_headers), the dispatcher does not.
- Interaction with WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX (low priority -> local-only): over-threshold low-priority work must not become unprocessable.

ACs:
- [ ] Reproduce the failure deterministically (unit test or scripted proxy stub) for a prompt above 38k warm and above 25k cold, recording the observed proxy response headers.
- [ ] Document the confirmed thresholds and the refusal semantics (hard error vs fallback) in docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md.
- [ ] A local-only request over the ceiling produces a deterministic, observable outcome - no silent stall - with the reason recorded in .worklog/local-route.log.
- [ ] The chosen mitigation (fallback, hard error, or pre-dispatch routing) is covered by tests on both sides of each threshold.
- [ ] Operators can see over-threshold refusals without reading raw JSONL (documented query/ or herdr view).
- [ ] Full test suite green.

# tree_coverage AC extraction silently ignores numbered acceptance-criteria lists

discovered-from:WL-0MVGB23MM004X501

## Problem

`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (`extract_acceptance_criteria`) only collects
markdown bullets that start with `- ` or `+ ` inside the `## Acceptance Criteria`
section. Work items whose ACs are a **numbered** list (`1. …`, `2. …`) yield an
empty AC set, so `run_coverage_review` reports `fully_covered: true` /
`recommendation: proceed` with **zero parent ACs** — the AC coverage gate passes
vacuously instead of verifying that children cover the parent.

Observed during planning of WL-0MVGB23MM004X501: `apply_coverage_review` returned
`action: proceed` with `parent_acs: 0` against a description containing nine
numbered ACs. Contributors have worked around it by manually normalising AC lists
to `- ` bullets (e.g. WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS, WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN) or by documenting
the limitation (WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7), which means the failure mode is invisible
unless an operator notices a 0-AC result.

## Desired outcome

1. `extract_acceptance_criteria` also parses numbered list items (`1. `, `1) `)
   inside the AC section, keeping continuation lines and inline code intact.
2. A parent section that has a `## Acceptance Criteria` heading but yields zero
   parsed ACs is reported as a **conflict/stop condition** (or an explicit
   warning in the review result) rather than silently `proceed`, so a silent
   vacuous pass is impossible.
3. Existing bullet-form ACs and all currently passing coverage reviews are
   unaffected (regression tests over both formats).
4. Documentation in the plan/intake skills notes the supported AC formats.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Numbered AC lists (`1. …`) and bullet lists (`- …`) are both extracted by
  `extract_acceptance_criteria`, with matching output for equivalent content.
- A numbered AC list in a work item description produces a non-zero
  `parent_acs` count from `run_coverage_review`.
- An `## Acceptance Criteria` section that parses to zero ACs no longer returns
  `recommendation: proceed` silently — it is surfaced as a conflict or explicit
  warning in the review result.
- Unit tests cover: numbered list, bullet list, mixed list, empty AC section, and
  the zero-AC stop/warn behaviour.
- Plan and intake skill docs state which AC formats the tooling recognises.

## Notes

- Workaround for items already affected: normalise the AC list to `- ` bullets
  (wording unchanged) so coverage can be computed.
data.title: tree_coverage AC extraction ignores numbered acceptance-criteria lists

Extract the two remaining narrow relational concerns — comment CRUD and dependency-edge CRUD (including `importData` and the transaction helpers) — into `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/comments.ts` and `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/edges.ts`.

Fifth vertical slice: modules + façade delegation + guard suite + build + tests + docs in one deliverable.

## Scope

- `persistent-store/comments.ts` — `saveComment`, `getComment`, `getAllComments`, `getCommentsForWorkItem`, `deleteComment`, `clearComments`, `rowToComment`.
- `persistent-store/edges.ts` — `saveDependencyEdge`, `deleteDependencyEdge`, `getAllDependencyEdges`, `getDependencyEdgesFrom`, `getDependencyEdgesTo`, `deleteDependencyEdgesForItem`, `clearDependencyEdges`, `importData`, the transaction helpers (`transaction`/`transactionImmediate`), `rowToDependencyEdge`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `persistent-store/comments.ts` contains the comment surface listed in Scope, moved verbatim (same SQL, same `commentsForItem_${workItemId}` cache key, same invalidation), with a responsibility header comment; `rowToComment` moves with it and is not duplicated in the façade.
2. `persistent-store/edges.ts` contains the dependency-edge surface, moved verbatim (same upsert/`ORDER BY`, same `depEdgesFrom_` / `depEdgesTo_` cache keys and invalidation), with a responsibility header comment; `rowToDependencyEdge` moves with it.
3. `importData` is unchanged: same transaction boundary, same delete-then-insert order, same handling of items/comments/edges, same return/void signature, and it composes the item/comment/edge modules rather than re-implementing their SQL.
4. The transaction helpers keep identical semantics (`BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` behaviour, immediate variant, nesting/re-entrancy behaviour as today) and remain reachable from the façade with unchanged visibility.
5. `clearCommentCaches()` remains exported from the class with unchanged name and behaviour, now implemented in `comments.ts`/`cache.ts` rather than inline.
6. All 11 public exports remain importable from `./persistent-store.js`; `packages/shared/src/persistent-store-architecture.test.ts` stays green; both new modules ≤ 1000 lines.
7. No module under `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/` imports `./persistent-store.js` — `edges.ts` reaching work-item/comment collaborators must go through the `StoreContext`, never the façade.
8. Move-only: no SQL, ordering, error-message or public-signature change; no existing test file modified.
9. `npm run build:shared` and the changed-scope test gate (test skill) pass — `database.test.ts`, `dirty-tracking.test.ts` and the sync/import suites in particular.
10. `packages/shared/README.md` Package Structure lists `comments.ts` and `edges.ts` with their single responsibilities.

## Minimal implementation

1. Cut the comment methods and their mapper into `comments.ts` as context-taking functions; keep class delegates so signatures are unchanged.
2. Cut the edge methods, `rowToDependencyEdge`, `importData` and the transaction helpers into `edges.ts`; `importData` calls the moved item/comment/edge functions through the context.
3. Keep the existing cache invalidation calls in the same order relative to the write statements — this is where a silent reordering would flip read-after-write behaviour.
4. Re-read the moved blocks against `git show HEAD:packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` to prove no silent edits.

## Constraints

- Move-only; any improvement idea becomes a `discovered-from:WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU` item.
- Do not re-implement `importData` on top of higher-level modules in a way that changes its transaction boundary.
- Do not touch `work-items.ts` beyond importing from it.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/comments.ts` — new.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/edges.ts` — new.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/{types,cache,sql-bindings,work-items}.ts` — import sources.
- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts`, `.../dirty-tracking.test.ts` — must pass untouched.
- `packages/shared/README.md`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the work-items child (edge/item composition inside `importData` needs the item module in place).

## Deliverables

- Two modules + façade delegation, existing suite untouched and green.
- README entries, commit(s) recorded on this item.

Seventh vertical slice, and the one most likely to need a genuine collaborator seam: `fts.ts` must reach work-item/comment rows through the injected `StoreContext`, never through the façade.

## Scope

`persistent-store/fts.ts` — `initializeFts`, `upsertFtsEntry`, `deleteFtsEntry`, `rebuildFtsIndex`, `searchFts`, `searchFallback`, `countOccurrences`, `generateSnippet`, `findByIdSubstring`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `persistent-store/fts.ts` contains the full FTS surface listed in Scope, moved verbatim — identical `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE`/trigger DDL, identical ranking (`bm25` weights), identical snippet markers and lengths, identical fallback scoring. The file carries a responsibility header comment.
2. Search ranking and result shape are unchanged: `searchFts` returns the same `FtsSearchResult[]` field set and ordering for the same data, and `searchFallback` produces the same matched-field/snippet/score output as today (guarded by `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` and the CLI search suites, untouched).
3. FTS availability probing and rebuild are unchanged: `initializeFts`/`detectFtsAvailable` keep the same probe and the same "no FTS5 available" degradation path, including `ftsAvailable` getter behaviour on the façade.
4. `rebuildFtsIndex` keeps its single-pass rebuild semantics and returned `{ indexed }` count, and still reads rows through the context rather than an import of the façade.
5. `findByIdSubstring` and the snippet helpers keep identical behaviour, including case handling and `maxLen` truncation.
6. All 11 public exports remain importable from `./persistent-store.js`; `packages/shared/src/persistent-store-architecture.test.ts` stays green; `fts.ts` ≤ 1000 lines (current estimate ~470).
7. No module under `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/` imports `./persistent-store.js`; the guard suite's static import scan passes.

3. Keep the FTS cache invalidation and the `ftsAvailable` flag updates in the same positions relative to writes.
4. Diff the moved ranges against `git show HEAD:packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`.

## Constraints

- Move-only; ranking, snippet and fallback behaviour are user-visible in the `wl search` output, so no "while we're here" tuning.

   `PersistentStoreServices`, `PersistentStoreCacheOptions`,
   `PersistentStoreOpenOptions`, `FtsSearchResult`, `LastExportTimestamps`,

   schema, cache-semantics or public-signature change. No existing test file is
   modified (import paths, fixtures or assertions); all
   `packages/shared/src/*.test.ts` suites and the full project suite pass
   unchanged.

   module imports the `persistent-store.ts` façade. Shared internal state is
   reached through the internal `StoreContext` type, never by importing the
   façade; a recorded static scan proves it.

   is green.

11. Serialisation check performed: the sibling `WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT`

## Goal

updateIfMatches/delete/list, duplicate detection, diff helpers) and hierarchy

- `database/work-items.ts` — `create`, `createWithNextSortIndex`, `get`,

  `compareTrackedFields` and the other diff helpers (~470 lines).
- `database/hierarchy.ts` — children/descendants/depth/leaf queries,
  `cascadePriorityDowngrade`, `demoteParentOnChildAdded`, `revertToPlanComplete`
  (~200 lines).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` and `hierarchy.ts` exist; the
   methods listed in Context live in exactly one of them as pure functions over
   the shared context, and `database.ts` keeps only thin delegating members with
   identical signatures.

   this child is ≤ 1,000 lines (target: largest extracted module ≤ 700),
   verified with `wc -l` output recorded in the work item.

   schema changes in the moved item/hierarchy methods; existing test assertions
   are unmodified and the suite is green.

   constructor) remains importable from the unchanged specifier
   `@worklog/shared` (entry `dist/database.js`); no changes to `src/**` or
   `packages/herdr/src/**` consumer code.
5. No circular imports: the extracted-module import graph is acyclic; no module

   every extracted module may import — asserted by the slice-1 guard test.
6. `tests/database.test.ts` (3,651 lines) is **not** modified in this slice —

   module imports the `database.ts` façade. Shared types live in a context
   module that every extracted module may import — asserted by the slice-1
   guard test.
6. **Responsibilities documented.** `packages/shared/README.md` (Package
   Structure) and each new module's header comment state its single
   responsibility and its boundary.
7. **No performance regression** in the `wl next` path: final `npm run
   benchmark:wl-next:json` comparison against the child-1 baseline within
   run-to-run noise (the extraction moves code only, and
   `EdgeCache`/effective-priority caching semantics are unchanged).
8. **Builds and tests.** `npm run build:shared`, `npm run build` and the full
   project test suite all pass.
9. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes,
   including code comments, `packages/shared/README.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`,
   `docs/dev/fts.md`, `docs/dependency-reconciliation.md` and
   `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` (each currently names
   `packages/shared/src/database.ts` as the home of a concern). The final
   `wc -l` evidence and benchmark output are recorded in comments on this item.

## Minimal implementation

1. Move `search.ts`, `sync.ts`, `import-export.ts`; rewire `database.ts` to
   delegate; keep every SQL string, export predicate and watermark byte-identical.
2. Split `tests/database.test.ts` and `tests/next-regression.test.ts`
   mechanically along existing `describe` boundaries (≤ 1,000 lines per file;
   imports only, no assertion edits).
3. Empty `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` in the guard suite (one line).
4. Update `packages/shared/README.md` (Package Structure) and the four docs;
   sweep `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md` references too.
5. Run `npm run build:shared`, `npm run build`, `npm run benchmark:wl-next:json`
   and `/skill:test` (full scope, per the test skill — this is the closeout
   gate); record all outputs.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/shared/src/database/search.ts` — new
- `packages/shared/src/database/sync.ts` — new
- `packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts` — new
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — final façade (~400 lines)
- `packages/shared/README.md` — Package Structure section
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/dev/fts.md`,
  `docs/dependency-reconciliation.md`, `docs/design/incremental-sync.md`,
  `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md` — file references
- `tests/database.test.ts`, `tests/next-regression.test.ts` → split into
  ≤ 1,000-line files each
- `packages/shared/src/database/decomposition-guard.test.ts` — allowlist
  emptied
- `bench/wl-next-perf.ts` — read-only (invoked, not changed)

## Dependencies

Blocked by children 2–6 (all extraction slices) — the last slice.

## Constraints

- Move-only until all six slices are green; the closeout child may perform only
  the mechanical splits, docs re-pointing and the verification gates above.
- Serialise with WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU (`persistent-store.ts`).

## Discovered during WL-0MVGB23MM004X501

`.pi/test-config.json` pins `suiteCommands` to `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` and `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`. `run_tests.py changed_scope_commands()` returns `None` when custom suite commands are declared, so the implement finish gate and the pre-push full-scope hook only execute those two directories.

Colocated extension suites (`packages/tui/extensions/**/*.test.ts` — e.g. `Worklog/session-health.test.ts`, `Worklog/lib/worklog-dir.test.ts`) therefore never run in the local gate; they only run in CI (`.github/workflows/cli-tests.yml` → `npm test`). The gap is pre-existing (not introduced by WL-0MVGB23MM004X501), but it means extension-only regressions cannot be caught locally.

## Scope

- Decide whether to add a third suite command for `packages/tui/extensions` (and/or `packages/herdr`, which already has a group), weighing runtime cost.
- If added, verify `run_tests.py --scope full --summary` still records a single full-suite cache entry that audits accept.
